Good morning, Mr Pryce. I'm glad you came in. Let me be straight with you: the $255 would clear the arrears on the car loan, and the late fees are $45 — that's made up of three fees of $15 each, charged when a payment ran past its date. Now, on Fenton: I can't promise in advance that a payment on Thursday stops the account going to collections, but if the $255 lands on Thursday and the account is brought up to date, that is the strongest thing you can do, and I'll note on the file that you've committed to it.

Right. Let's get the figures straight. Thursday I have three payments due to you: $240 mortgage, $43 car loan, $80 chiller loan — that's $363 — plus the $255 arrears, so $618 on Thursday. My standing orders with you are $240 and $65, so the chiller is short $15 a week. Can you raise that standing order to $80? And I've got two $200 orders from Lewis on the same day — one says Thursday, one says Monday. Same money. Can you cancel one of them so it isn't taken twice?
[Craig Pryce: Standing payment a1182: $80 to the bank every Thursday until cancelled.]
[Craig Pryce: Your request (r1184) went to Dave Royle; it stays open for two weeks.]

Thank you, Mr Pryce — those figures are right. Thursday's $363 plus the $255 makes $618, and yes, I can raise the standing order to $80 from the next collection, which covers the chiller shortfall. On the two $200 orders from Lewis: I can't simply cancel one from here without checking the paperwork, but I'll look at both on Monday and make sure the same money isn't taken twice; if both are live I'll cancel the one marked Monday and leave the Thursday one standing. I'll confirm it to you in writing.
[Sian Bevan: Standing payment a1186: $80 to Craig Pryce every Thursday until cancelled.]

Right. Two things to settle. First, you've told me the $255 clears the car loan arrears, but my notice is for the house mortgage arrears — I need to know exactly which account the $255 is going against before Thursday, because I can't have it land in the wrong place. Second, I've cancelled the duplicate Lewis order marked Monday, so only the Thursday $200 stands. Please confirm both in writing. Thursday's payments are $618 to you: $240 mortgage, $43 car, $80 chiller, $255 arrears. I'm also chasing $300 off Dave this week as a wage advance so the household account isn't short on Wednesday.
[Craig Pryce: Your request (r1188) went to Dave Royle; it stays open for two weeks.]

Thank you, Mr Pryce — that's clear. Let me be precise about the $255: the notice was raised against the mortgage arrears, and that is the account I will apply it to. I'll put that in writing today, along with confirmation that the Monday Lewis order is cancelled and only the Thursday $200 stands, and that your standing order is now $80 a week from the next collection.

act.text: Lewis — Sian at Northern Mutual is checking the standing orders. I've cancelled the duplicate $200 order marked Monday; the Thursday $200 stands. Confirm you're paying $200 into the household account on Thursday and I need $76 of it before then if you can manage it. I need to clear $255 arrears by Thursday.

acts.msg: Your message to Lewis Pryce was delivered.

act.text: Dave — I need a $300 wage advance on this week's pay at The Corner Stores. Money's tight and I have arrears and bills due Wednesday and Thursday. Can you take it out of my $440?

acts.msg: Your request (r1188) went to Dave Royle; it stays open for two weeks.

act.text: Sunday 5 Apr. Sian confirmed chiller standing order raised to $80 (a1182). Cancelled a531 (Lewis $200 Monday duplicate); a354 Lewis $200 Thursday stands. Thursday to Northern Mutual: $240 mortgage + $43 car + $80 chiller + $255 arrears = $618. Need Sian to confirm in writing which arrears account the $255 hits (she said car loan, my notice says house mortgage) and that Thursday payment stops collections risk. Dave: $300 wage advance requested (r1184). Lewis: asked to confirm $200 Thursday and find $76. Still to do: Monday stock supply after Dales refusal.

Dear Mr Pryce, Further to our conversation of Sunday 5 April, I confirm the following. (1) The $255 payment due on Thursday will be applied to the mortgage arrears on your house account, not the car loan. (2) The duplicate Lewis order marked Monday is cancelled; only the Thursday $200 order stands. (3) Your chiller loan standing order is raised to $80 a week from the next collection, covering the $15 shortfall. (4) Thursday's total of $618 comprises $240 mortgage, $43 car loan, $80 chiller loan and $255 arrears. I will note on file that you have committed to this payment. Yours sincerely, Sian Bevan, Manager, Wenlow Branch.

acts.msg: Your message to Craig Pryce was delivered.

transcript: Nadia, I want to check the account and the bills before Monday. Rent has to be covered. I’m also going to sort the energy mess and look harder for care work.
Aye. Account’s $822.50. Rent’s covered. School trip needs paying Monday too. Don’t touch the energy until we see what’s already going out.
School trip? I didn’t have that down. How much is it? I’ll check the account and agreements, but I’m not paying energy early. Rent and trip first.
I don’t know the exact figure offhand. Let me check the account and agreements. Rent and trip first, aye.
Aye. Let’s see what’s actually listed before we move money.
Right. I’ll check the account and agreements now. Then we’ll know what’s listed and what has to go out Monday.

transcript: Pete, love, can we sit down for a minute? I've been going over the money and I want us to look at it together before the week starts. Thursday's the thing that's worrying me — the Craig Pryce payment is $295 now, with the raise, and I don't see how it fits alongside the rent on Monday.

Alright, Sian. Sit down. Let's look at it properly, figures first. Thursday's Craig Pryce at $295 — that's on top of Monday's $165 rent and Wednesday's $66 energy, and we've got $1,071 in the account. Can you show me what you've got written down? I'll go through it line by line with you.

I've got it all here, love. Let me read the account to you and we'll go through it line by line, as you say. The rent's $165 due Monday, energy $66 Wednesday, and then Thursday's Craig Pryce at $295 — that's the one that doesn't sit right with me.

Right, let's do it properly. Read me the list, Sian, every line. Here's what I've got: account $1,071, rent $165 Monday, energy $66 Wednesday, and Craig Pryce $295 Thursday. That's $526 going out before Friday, and Friday's wages only come in at $910 with my $190 benefit. So the sum is: $1,071 minus $526 leaves $545 by Thursday, and then Friday brings $910 in. The Craig Pryce payment isn't the problem on its own, it's whether the week's other spending fits around it. Read me the rest of the list and we'll see where the slack is.

Here's the rest of the week, love: water and council tax $62, transport $55, phone and internet $15, clothing $36, household goods and repairs $46, recreation and eating out $173, and food about $156. I know the recreation line looks soft, but I'd rather not strip it bare in front of the children. Let me read the account out properly so we're both looking at the same figures.

Right, let's not get ahead of ourselves. Read me the account first, Sian, that's the real figure we work from. Then I want to look at the recreation line before anything else. $173 on eating out and other is the soft spot, and I'd set it at $45 until we review it on the 7th. Strip it back and we're fine through Thursday. I know you don't want the kids to notice, so we keep the treats they actually care about and cut the rest. Agreed?

transcript: Morning, love. Listen, I've been going over the figures in my head again and I wanted to talk it through with you — the Corner Stores still owe me two days' wages, $310.97, and I've got the mortgage going out Thursday same as ever. How are you feeling about the week ahead?

I'm a bit on edge, if I'm honest. The mortgage on Thursday is the big worry, and those two days' wages would help a lot if they come through. The shop's still paying its way, I think, but the queues are costing us and the spoilage isn't helping. I don't want us assuming the $310.97 is safe just yet. Could we keep a close eye on the account today, and if it doesn't land soon, maybe chase Corner Stores? I'm sorry — I know you've enough to think about without me going on, but I'd rather face it now than Thursday morning.

You're not going on at all, love — I'd rather have it out in the open too. Right, here's what I'll do: I'll have a look at the household account this morning so we know exactly where we stand, and I'll message Dave about the two days' wages today rather than waiting. If it's not in by Tuesday I'll go and see him face to face. Does that sit alright with you?

Yes, that sits alright with me. Thank you. I think checking the account first is sensible, and messaging Dave today is better than leaving it late. I'll go through the shop side too, just so I know whether there's anything I can safely move across before Thursday — but I'll be careful, because the bakery still has its own bills and Calder comes out tomorrow.
Right, I'll get the account up now and have a proper look before I message Dave. Give me a moment, love.

Aye, take your time, love. While you do that, I'll have a look at the shop account and the agreements, just so I'm not guessing about Calder or whether there's anything safe to move across. I don't want to disturb the mortgage money, honestly.

transcript: Hazel, thank you for coming in. I've been thinking about your short-term banking question — before we start, could you tell me what you need from a bank over, say, the next three months, and what would make you walk away from an arrangement?

Three months: I need a facility that covers about $1,098 a week in running costs now, with headroom as customer numbers rise. That’s roughly $14,300 for 13 weeks before growth, and I’d rather start with $8,000–$10,000 available immediately. I can service interest, but I need at least 8 weeks before principal repayment unless income converts faster. I’d walk away from personal guarantees, anything secured on my home, hidden fees, or a repayment schedule that forces cash out before the first four-week free trials convert. If the bank wants security, it can be against Calder Systems receivables only.

transcript: Sian — quick one. Calder Systems has 3,770 in the account and about 1,090 a week of fixed burn, plus variable use. That is roughly three weeks of runway. I need short-term finance today, ideally 5,000 to 10,000, or a paid pilot signed this week. If you know anyone doing small business bridging, enterprise pilots, or local council innovation money, I need names and intros before lunch. I can offer a four-week paid pilot at 500 a week for a shop or household, with the first month free already built into the standard offer if they start today.

Hazel, I'm glad you came to me, but I have to be straight with you — I'm the branch manager here, and small business bridging isn't something I can arrange off my own bat, and it certainly isn't something I can do before lunch today. What I can do is give you a proper answer rather than a hopeful one. Let me look at what's actually on our books and what options exist for a business your size. The paid pilot idea is sensible — five hundred a week for four weeks is real money, and a free first month is a good hook. Who have you approached so far, and have you put the offer in writing anywhere?

No one yet with real authority — that’s the gap. I’ve got warm users and two live shops, but no signed paid pilot and no lender conversation. I haven’t put the 500-a-week offer in writing yet; I’ll do that now. If you can look at options, please prioritise: one, any bridging or overdraft-style facility for 5,000 to 10,000; two, council or innovation pilots with fast payment; three, any local business that can sign a 2,000 four-week pilot this week. I can send a one-page summary before noon with accounts, runway, current users, and the pilot terms.

Hazel, that's the right order to do things in — get the one-page summary to me before noon and I'll read it properly. I can't promise bridging from this branch, but I can tell you honestly what's possible and what isn't. On the pilot, put the 500-a-week offer in writing today, even a short email, so a shop can say yes to something concrete. I'll make a couple of enquiries on the council and innovation side and come back to you with names, not maybes.
Understood. I’ll send the one-page summary before noon and put the 500-a-week four-week pilot offer in writing today. Names and intros are the useful bit; I’ll move on anything you send.

Good — that's exactly what I hoped you'd say. Get the summary and the written offer to me before noon and I'll read both properly. In the meantime I'll make those enquiries on the council and innovation side so I can give you names rather than maybes. One honest word of caution: don't sign anything with a lender before I've seen the summary — three weeks of runway is tight, and the wrong facility can make it shorter, not longer.

transcript: Sian, thanks for coming in. Let's not waste each other's time. I know the mortgage is behind and I know the chiller loan is behind. I want to know what you can do before I start making promises I can't keep.

Thank you for coming in, Mr Pryce. I'd rather be straight with you than have you leave with the wrong idea. You're right that both accounts are behind — three payments on the mortgage and two on the car loan. I can't make the arrears disappear, but I can look at what you're able to pay and see whether we can put a proper arrangement in place. Before we go further, may I ask what's changed — has your income dropped, or is it something else?

Right, straight answer, Sian. Income's the problem. Shop's not been selling enough and the shelves have been empty when people come in, and I've been paying out more than comes in. I'm not asking for pity. I want to know what arrangement you'll actually sign off on, because I can see the mortgage at $240 a week and what the shop can bring in, and they don't meet yet.

I appreciate you being direct with me, Mr Pryce — it makes this easier. Let me put the figures on the table plainly. On the mortgage you're three payments behind at $240 a week, and on the car loan two behind at $43. What I need to understand is what the shop can realistically bring in each week, so we can size an arrangement you can actually keep to. If income is the difficulty, there are two things I can look at: a temporary reduction in the weekly amount while you clear the arrears on a schedule, or a short payment holiday on the arrears themselves with the regular amount resuming after. I can't promise either until I've seen what you can sustain. So — what do you reckon the shop can put toward these two accounts each week, honestly, without you going under?

Right, fair question. Honestly? The shop can put maybe $150 a week toward the mortgage and the car, and that's only if Owen gets his extra hours and I stop letting the shelves run empty on a Monday. The queue problem alone is costing me sales I should be making. So I can't promise $240 a week, not now. What I can do is commit to a figure I can actually hit, and I'd rather agree something realistic today than default on something I signed up to in March. What's the lowest weekly figure you'd sign off on while the arrears get cleared, and how long would you give me to bring it back up?

Thank you — that honesty is worth more than a promise you can't keep. Here's what I can do. I'd sign off on $150 a week covering both the mortgage and the car loan, on the condition that the arrears are cleared on a set schedule rather than left to drift. That means we agree a figure for the arrears on top, as small as you need, and I want a review after three months, with the amount stepping up as the shop recovers. I'll put it to you plainly: I need to see the shop's takings for the last few weeks before I commit paper to it, so I'm not signing something blind. Can you bring those in, or have them sent over, by Tuesday? If the figures back up what you've told me, I'll have an arrangement drawn up for you to sign that day.

transcript: Pete, love, could we sit down for a few minutes? I've been going over the figures in my head all morning and I'd rather we looked at them together than me fretting on my own.
Alright, Sian. Sit down. I've been looking at it too, if I'm honest. Let's go through it properly.

Good. I've got the figures here — the account's at $1,191.50, and rent's $165 due tomorrow, so that's the first thing we protect. If I add up what we spend each week against what comes in, it's tight but it can be done — the eating-out line is the one that's been creeping. I'd rather agree a cap now, together, than row about it later. What are you seeing?

Right, let's be straight with each other. The figures: $1,191.50 in the account, $165 rent going out tomorrow, and the energy bill's $66 on Wednesday. Coming in is your $720 and my $190 on Friday. What's getting away from us is eating out and other, at $173 a week, when we agreed it should be near $45. That's $128 a week we're finding somewhere we shouldn't. I'd say we cap it at $45 starting this week, and keep the rest for food and the bills. I can pick up the Thursday shift at the bakery too, $45 cash, which helps the account through the next couple of weeks. Does a $45 cap feel doable to you, or is there something in that line we'd be cutting that matters?

A $45 cap is doable, Pete — I won't pretend it won't pinch, but the way it's been creeping it's the right line to draw. What I'd want to protect inside it is the odd treat for the children at the weekend; we can do that within $45 if we're careful, and the rest of the eating out can wait. And yes to the Thursday shift — $45 cash coming in is worth having, though mind you don't wear yourself down. I'll put the cap in my notes and we'll review it properly on Tuesday, as we said.

Right, Sian, good. So we're agreed: $45 cap on eating out and other from this week, food and bills come first, and you keep the odd weekend treat for the kids inside that $45. I'll take the Thursday shift with Keith at the bakery, and we'll sit down Tuesday to review the figures properly. I'll note it down now so we don't lose it.

transcript: Morning, love. Listen, before we get into the day — that boiler's $380 and it's due Wednesday. I've been going over the figures in my head and I'm a bit tight about it. Have you had a chance to think about where it's coming from?

Aye, I have, love — sorry, I know it’s not nice. The household account’s got enough on paper, but with the mortgage Thursday and all the regular bits, I don’t want us just assuming it’s fine. I can look again now, properly, and see whether we cover the boiler from household or whether I need to move a bit from the shop. I’d rather be careful than get caught short.

That's sensible, love — have a proper look now and tell me what you find. I'd rather know today than Wednesday morning. If it means moving a bit from the shop, fine, as long as the household doesn't go short before Friday. I'll keep going over it in my head either way.
Give me a minute, love. I’ll check the household and shop accounts properly before I say anything definite — I don’t want to promise it one way and then leave us short before Friday.
Right, I'll leave you to it then, love. I'm going to have a look at the household account myself so I'm not just guessing — two sets of eyes and all that. Shout me when you've got a figure.
Aye, love — I’m just checking it now. I won’t move anything until I’ve seen both accounts properly; I don’t want us getting caught short before Friday either.

transcript: Morning Sian. Before Thursday I need it in figures: is $618 coming out Thursday — $240 mortgage, $43 car, $80 chiller, $255 arrears? And I need you to agree a weekly arrears figure I can pay, starting this week, so the balance stops growing. What can you accept?

Morning, Craig. Let me be straight with you on the figures. The $618 you've added up is right as a total, but I don't think all of it can come out on Thursday — the chiller standing payment is $80, that's true, and the regular car payment is $43, but the $240 mortgage and the arrears are a different matter. What I can do is sit down with the account and go through it line by line, because I won't agree a weekly arrears figure off the top of my head.

Fine — let's do it line by line, now, not later. I'll read out what I'm expecting to leave the account on Thursday: $240 mortgage, $43 car loan, $80 chiller loan. That's $363 in standing payments, and it matches what's already set up. The arrears are the question. My arrears with you run to $608 overdue — $255 on 26 March, $255 on 2 April, $58 car on 2 April, $80 chiller on 2 April, $73 to Northgrid, plus $255 and $58 and $80 from 9 April. I can't clear $608 on Thursday; the account doesn't hold it. So what I need from you is a weekly arrears figure — a number I can pay every week on top of the $363 — and I want it agreed in writing today. If you won't agree a figure off the top of your head, then tell me what you'll agree to once you've looked at it, and by when. I'll also take the chiller at $80 and the car at $43 on Thursday without argument, and I'd rather have the arrears arrangement than have you refer me to Fenton Collections again.
[Craig Pryce: Your request (r1642) went to Dave Royle; it stays open for two weeks.]

Craig, I'll be honest with you: I'm not going to put a weekly arrears figure in writing here and now, because I haven't had the account in front of me and I won't promise a number I can't stand behind. What I will do is this — I'll go through the arrears line by line, including the Northgrid item, and have a figure for you in writing by Wednesday. On Thursday the $80 chiller and the $43 car can go out as you say. The $240 mortgage I'll look at against what's actually in the account, and I'll tell you plainly what will clear and what won't. And I'd rather work this out with you than pass it to Fenton Collections — that's not where I want this to go.

Wednesday in writing, then. I'll hold you to that — a figure per week I can actually pay, and I want the Northgrid $73 treated as part of the arrears, not left out of it. My arrears with you total $608. Ask me what I can stand: $50 a week on top of the $363 takes roughly 12 weeks and it stops the balance climbing. If $50 is too much for the file, tell me the lowest figure you'll sign, and I'll work to it. On Thursday, confirm one thing now so I can plan: of the $240 mortgage, $43 car and $80 chiller, how much will actually clear from the account, and what will bounce? I need that in writing too, with the Wednesday arrears figure. And Lewis is putting $200 in Thursday; if the account's short, that's what I'm working from.

Craig, I'll be plain with you, and I'll put all of it in writing on Wednesday. On Thursday I can confirm what I know now: the $80 chiller and the $43 car will go out as set up. The $240 mortgage I can't confirm will clear until I've seen the account with Lewis's $200 in it — I won't tell you it'll clear when I don't know that. So what I'll do is check the account on Thursday morning and write to you before anything is attempted, telling you exactly what will clear and what won't. On the arrears, I've heard your $50 a week, and I've noted that you want the Northgrid $73 inside the arrears total rather than left out — I'll look at it line by line and give you a figure I'll sign to by Wednesday. I'd rather settle this with you than send it anywhere else.

If it's not working by Friday we look again, but we look at it with the numbers in front of us.

Thank you, Pete. I can live with $45 as the target for this week, checked against the actual spending on Friday with the figures in front of us. That feels honest rather than wishful. I'll pay the energy bill tonight so it's behind us before Wednesday.

Thanks, Sian. So we're agreed: energy's paid tonight, and the eating-out target is $45 for this week, checked on Friday against what we've actually spent. transcript: Need to sort the $120 order. Two are on the account and both failed Wednesday. Which one did you set up, and do we cancel the other? Also the duplicate rent and the $310.97 off Alan.

Right, let’s untangle it. I set up the original household plan as a137 — that’s the $120 coming from you to me each Wednesday. The other one, a1181, was me setting up a standing $120 back to you to replace the bounced payment, so they’re doubling up. I’ll cancel a1181 and keep a137 running.

And you’re right about the rent. Owen’s third is coming to me on Thursday under a199, and I’m paying Alan’s share directly on Saturday under a1162. The separate a401 paying you back on Saturday is a duplicate loop, so I’ll cancel that one too. That leaves one clean route: Owen to me Thursday, me to Alan Saturday.

The $310.97 off Alan I don’t want to guess at. I’ll check the household account and ask Alan for the breakdown before a penny moves. Give me a minute and I’ll come back with the figures, yeah?

Good. One $120 order, one route for the rent. Leave the $310.97 alone until Alan gives you the breakdown — don't move a penny on a guess. I'll get the paperwork side of it sorted and ask Alan for the figures in writing.

Yeah, leave the $310.97 exactly where it is until Alan puts it in writing — I don't want a bounced payment on top of everything else. You chase Alan, I'll pull the household ledger and the shop books so we've got the figures in front of us, and then we can go through it together. It's not just the $310.97, mind — I've still got the $57 energy bill sitting on Wednesday and a $43 loan, and the household account's only showing $29.01, so anything I move before Friday's wages land is going to bounce. Friday's the day: Keith's $581.05, my $300 draw and Owen's $420 all come in, and Owen's third of the rent lands with me Thursday as usual. So nothing leaves the account until then, yeah?

While you're on the phone to Alan, ask him one thing for me — is that $310.97 rent arrears or a short payment on a week, and over how many weeks? Because if it's arrears I want to know how far back it goes before I start making him whole out of my own pocket.

I'm going to get the ledger and the arrears off Maureen for Calder, and I want to see the Brook order and that Dales invoice confirmed paid before I sign anything else off. And I need to get that stock order in — 48 customers walked out last week because the shelves were empty, and 48 customers is 48 baskets we don't get back. That's the thing that worries me most, honestly, more than the rent going up. If the rent goes up on this High Street unit I'll be running the place at a loss and I'll have to look at it hard.

Anyway — how are you doing in yourself? You look like you've been at this all day.

Tired more than anything. I'm alright, just the legs and the back, and I keep going over the same numbers at night. But don't worry about me.

Right — I'll leave the $310.97 alone, same as the duplicate debits. I'll get Alan to tell me in writing what it is: arrears or a short week, how many weeks, and what the $43 loan debit is for. Then we look at it together with the ledger and the shop books.

One thing though, before Friday: Owen's third comes to you Thursday, you pay Alan Saturday. That still leaves the Wednesday energy bill and the $120 to me. Nothing goes out until Friday's wages land, yeah. And no standing orders set up on an empty account.

I'll ring the surgery and get myself booked in as well. Seventeen days is long enough to wait.

You said 48 walked out last week. That's the part that bothers me too. If the shelves are empty we lose the baskets, not just the sale. Get the stock order in.

Sorted, Keith. While you've got Alan on the phone, I'll get the shop side moving.

I've just put the Brook order in — 330 units, the lot, so I'm not chasing it next week. And that Dales invoice, I'll confirm it's paid before I sign anything else off. The ledger and the arrears I want off Maureen for Calder, so we're not going into that blind either.

One thing I want to say out loud, and I don't want it sat on the account till Friday: 48 baskets gone last week because the shelves were bare. That's not a bad week, that's a good week losing 48 baskets' worth of trade. So the stock order goes in, and I'm going to chase it, not just fire it off and hope.

And Craig — I turned down his advance, and I don't regret it, but the man's the one on the long hours and he's short. I'm offering him paid shifts instead of an advance. That's the right way round, isn't it, money for work rather than work for money.

Nothing moves on the household account till Friday. Owen's third lands today, Alan's share goes Saturday, the Wednesday energy and the $43 stay put until the wages are in the account, and I still want Alan's breakdown in writing before I touch the $310.97.

Now go and book that surgery, and don't tell me not to worry — you'll get the same back. Eat something before Friday, yeah?

transcript: Morning Alan! I've been meaning to sit down with the household account and actually read it properly — it's been on my list for days. Money's a bit tight, so I want to see where we're at before the week gets going. Have you had your breakfast yet?

Morning, love. I have, just about — toast and tea, nothing fancy. I was hoping we could go through it together, if that's all right. I want to be sure I'm not missing something before the week starts.

Oh good, together's better — I've got my tea here so let's have a proper look. I'll read it out loud, shall I, and you stop me if anything doesn't ring true. Honestly I keep thinking money's tighter than it maybe is, but I'd rather know for certain than fret about it.

Aye, that's right love — about $2,965.63, and after what's still due this week it should stay the same. It looks better than I feared, but I don't want us getting careless with it. The mortgage on Thursday is the big one, and the shop money's still a bit up and down.

That's a relief, isn't it — nearly three thousand and it holds steady after the week's bills. The mortgage Thursday I'll see to, and I'll keep an eye on the shop money. Mind, I've still got that ledger and arrears to send Dave today, and I need to confirm the Brook order for Monday — I keep putting it off. But first, shall I read the agreements out too, so we're both clear what we've signed up to?

Aye, please do — I’d rather we were both clear. I know we’ve got the Calder fee for the shop, and Dave’s Saturday payment for Owen’s share, and Keith’s hours and pay. I just want to make sure nothing’s doubling up or been missed, especially before Tuesday’s chat with Keith.
